executive_summary: fleet-dashboard.cjs's printInbox() (the coordinator-audience inbox render) stamps read_at on every render with no idempotency gate, unlike every other write site cataloged in the consumption-semantics census -- so read_at drifts from 'first delivered' to 'most recently rendered' for this one site. Separately, the fleet-worker-loop-directive.md's 'READ-ONLY VIEW... stamps NOTHING' framing, while textually naming the worker-only renderer, invites a reader to generalize to the whole inbox command, which is false for the coordinator-audience path. Both are fixed here; verified safe (the SELECT no longer depends on read_at, so gating the UPDATE cannot reopen the RCA this write's own header comment cites).

functional_requirements.title: printInbox() stamps read_at idempotently, once per row
functional_requirements.description: scripts/fleet-dashboard.cjs:1911-1916's UPDATE currently has no read_at IS NULL gate. Add one, matching the established pattern at every other census-cataloged write site (solomon-advisory.cjs, adam-advisory.cjs, michael-inbox.cjs). Register the site in docs/protocol/coordinator-adam-comms.md's consumption-semantics census AND its regression-guard test's allowlist proactively, in the same PR -- learned directly from this session's own CI-caught miss on SD-LEO-INFRA-MICHAEL-ADAM-COMMS-001, where skipping this step failed session-coordination-consumption-census.test.js only after a push.
acceptance_criteria: printInbox's UPDATE gates on `.is('read_at', null)` in addition to `.in('id', ids)`.
A test asserts a fixture row already carrying a read_at value keeps that exact value after printInbox renders it again -- the timestamp is never overwritten.
A test asserts a fixture row with read_at NULL gets it stamped on first render (first-delivery semantics preserved).

functional_requirements.title: Correct the fleet-worker-loop-directive.md 'stamps nothing' framing to be precise
functional_requirements.description: docs/protocol/fleet-worker-loop-directive.md:55 states the inbox command 'is a READ-ONLY VIEW' and that printWorkerInbox 'stamps NOTHING' -- accurate for printWorkerInbox specifically, but the surrounding framing invites generalizing to the whole command, which is false for the coordinator-audience path (printInbox, reached whenever resolveInboxAudience() does not resolve to worker mode). Reword to name the coordinator-audience exception explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: The directive's wording for line 55 (or its replacement) names the coordinator-audience write path as the exception to the read-only framing, not just printWorkerInbox by name without context.

A diff review confirms the worker-facing guidance (use /checkin to drain, dashboard for viewing) is otherwise unchanged -- this is a precision correction, not a behavior change to the directive's actual instructions.

technical_requirements.description: No schema changes. session_coordination.read_at already exists and the idempotent-stamp pattern is already established elsewhere in this exact file family.

Verified safe: the SELECT feeding printInbox (fleet-dashboard.cjs:1814) gates on acknowledged_at, not read_at, so gating the UPDATE on read_at IS NULL cannot reopen the RCA (SD-LEO-INFRA-SIGNAL-INBOX-DRAIN-ON-DISPLAY-001) the write's header comment cites.
Both fixes are additive/behavioral-only inside existing functions plus one doc-file edit -- no new production files beyond tests.

test_scenarios.scenario: printInbox renders a row whose read_at is already set to a known past timestamp
test_scenarios.expected: The row's read_at is unchanged after the render -- the UPDATE's read_at IS NULL gate excludes it.

test_scenarios.expected: read_at is stamped to now() -- first-delivery semantics preserved, matching every other census site.

risks.risk: Gating the UPDATE on read_at IS NULL could theoretically reopen the 'filtered/parked render silently hides an unacked signal' bug this write's header comment cites as the reason it was made unconditional.
risks.mitigation: TR-2 verifies this is safe: that bug was fixed by changing the SELECT's gating column from read_at to acknowledged_at (fleet-dashboard.cjs:1814), so the read path no longer depends on read_at at all -- confirmed by reading the SELECT directly before scoping this SD.
